blocks.title: Why Build a RAG App with LlamaIndex matters here

spans.text: Problem statement: A LlamaIndex onboarding assistant must answer handbook questions with page-level evidence. The learner's job is not to memorize Build a RAG App with LlamaIndex; it is to decide what to build or change, what evidence the system may use, and how to tell whether the change improved answer groundedness and source coverage.

Running case: LlamaIndex index, query engine, and citation validation plan. We will keep this same case through the lesson so each idea has a job: frame the problem, explain the mechanism, choose a design, test the implementation, and decide what to do next.

Before reading on, predict: if metadata is lost, so answers cannot point back to the handbook section, where would you look first - the input, the state or data, the model boundary, the validation check, or the release process?
The lesson assumes you can learn the vocabulary, then spends its effort on integration choices, failure signals, and checks that make the idea usable in a real system.

blocks.title: Fully worked example: LlamaIndex index, query engine, and citation validation plan

spans.text: Scenario: A LlamaIndex onboarding assistant must answer handbook questions with page-level evidence. The team wants to improve answer groundedness and source coverage, but it has already seen this failure: metadata is lost, so answers cannot point back to the handbook section.
Here is the worked artifact at design-review depth: concrete enough to inspect, small enough to build as a thin slice.
Complete worked artifact

items.text: Question: "Can I get a refund after 35 days if I lost my invoice?" The answer must cite the exact policy chunk, not a plausible refund rule remembered by the model.

Artifact: LlamaIndex index, query engine, and citation validation plan. It specifies loaders, chunk metadata, retriever settings, prompt contract, citation format, and a faithfulness check for answer groundedness and source coverage.
Worked output: retrieve policy-refunds-v3 section 4, quote "30 days" and "invoice id required", answer that the request probably fails the policy, and link the source chunk used.

spans.text: Complete AI-assistant prompt for this artifact

Role: RAG reviewer. Context: A LlamaIndex onboarding assistant must answer handbook questions with page-level evidence. Task: inspect LlamaIndex index, query engine, and citation validation plan. Require a user question, retrieved chunks with source ids, final answer, and a claim-by-claim support check. Constraints: do not allow claims that are absent from retrieved chunks; flag stale or missing metadata. Output: {question, retrieved_sources, answer, unsupported_claims, release_decision}.
Why this is richer than a definition
The example ties Build a RAG App with LlamaIndex to a specific input, output, decision, failure mode, and metric. That is the move you should repeat when applying the lesson to your own system.

blocks.title: Case study: what changed after the first review

spans.text: The first prototype works on the demo path. Then a reviewer runs the uncomfortable case: metadata is lost, so answers cannot point back to the handbook section. The output still looks confident, which is exactly why the lesson needs a richer artifact.

The team does not restart from scratch. It adds one missing control to LlamaIndex index, query engine, and citation validation plan: a stricter input contract, better source metadata, a validation assertion, a human-review edge, a rollback trigger, or an audit log depending on where the failure appeared.

items.text: Decision made: keep the thin slice, but block release until the failure is observable and repeatable.
Evidence added: the artifact now shows the input, intermediate evidence, final output, and pass/fail reason.

blocks.title: How this breaks in practice

spans.text: The failure mode to keep in view is concrete: metadata is lost, so answers cannot point back to the handbook section. Use it as a diagnostic lens while reading every design choice.

items.text: Retrieved chunks mention the right keyword but not the answer-bearing paragraph.
The answer is relevant but unfaithful: it adds a policy or fact not present in the retrieved evidence.
Metadata is missing, so citations cannot be checked or reranked later.
The broad warning sign: answer groundedness and source coverage gets worse even though the final answer or artifact still looks polished.

spans.text: Debugging rule: inspect the earliest place where bad evidence can enter and the latest place where validation should have stopped it.
